sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and piece size
sections.what: Describes the file's job of hashing and checking encodings in bounded pieces, and sets the piece size to one megabyte.
sections.why: Keeps memory use flat for large uploads.

sections.name: SourceReadCancelled
sections.title: Cancellation error type
sections.what: Defines a specific error raised when the user cancels during reading of a source file.
sections.why: Lets the caller tell a cancellation apart from a real failure.

sections.name: _check_cancelled
sections.title: Checking for cancellation
sections.what: Asks the cancel check whether to stop, and if so raises the cancellation error with the name of the current stage.
sections.why: Lets long reads stop promptly while still saying what stage they were in.
sections.watch_out: The check runs once per piece, so cancellation takes effect only after the current megabyte is read.

sections.name: SourceFingerprint
sections.title: Source fingerprint record
sections.what: A small fixed record holding a file's SHA-256 hash, byte size and detected encoding.
sections.why: Gives callers one tidy result instead of loose values.

sections.name: _valid_for_encoding
sections.title: Testing an encoding across a file
sections.what: Checks whether a whole file decodes in a given encoding, reading it in pieces and stopping at the first invalid piece.
sections.why: Lets the encoding be chosen without loading the file into memory.

sections.name: fingerprint_text_file
sections.title: Fingerprinting and choosing a text encoding
sections.what: Hashes the whole text file and picks its encoding by trying UTF-8 (honouring a byte-order mark), then cp1252, then latin-1. It raises an error if none fits.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fallback order tries the most likely encodings first.
sections.watch_out: Because latin-1 accepts every byte, the error at the end is effectively unreachable.

sections.name: fingerprint_binary_file
sections.title: Fingerprinting a binary file
sections.what: Hashes a non-text file such as a spreadsheet and returns its hash and size, checking for cancellation between pieces.
sections.why: Binary files have no text encoding, so only the hash and size matter.

summary: Fingerprints text and binary source files in bounded pieces, and works out which text encoding a text file uses.
purpose: Lets the app identify each upload and read its text correctly, without loading the whole file into memory.
why: Schedule exports come from older tools in varied encodings. Trying encodings in a fixed order gives the most faithful reading. Reading in pieces keeps memory use flat.
how: Text files are read in one-megabyte pieces to build a SHA-256 hash and size. A byte-order mark is checked first. Then the whole file is checked in UTF-8, cp1252 and latin-1, in that order, and the first that decodes cleanly wins. Each pass checks for cancellation between pieces.
inputs: A file path and an optional cancel check.
outputs: A fingerprint with hash, size and detected encoding for text, or a hash and size for binary files.
risks: Because latin-1 accepts every byte, the last fallback never fails. A cp1252 file may therefore be read with characters that differ from the author's intent.
debug: If a file reads as garbled characters, check which encoding was chosen. If cancellation seems slow, check the piece size, since cancel is only checked between pieces.
